ca_wreckage_wall.blurb: Wreckage Wall is a bolted sport wall in the old quarry at Auburn State Recreation Area, reached by walking uphill past the lower-level climbs. The seventeen routes stretch from easy 5.7 to a handful of 5.12s, with the bulk sitting around 5.11. Expect lines of roughly fifty feet with slabs, arêtes, overhangs and some odd features, all ending at lowering anchors. Quarry rock can be loose, so tread carefully near the base and keep helmets on. The wall bakes in the sun on hot summer afternoons, so cooler seasons or early and late hours are more pleasant. A popular spot with a short slab for newer leaders and harder tests for stronger ones.

ca_slab_city_left.blurb: Slab City (Left) is the far-left stretch of the quarry in Riverside, a short-route sector built mostly around bolted slab climbing. Most of its seventeen climbs are sport, with one trad line and one aid line mixed in. Grades run from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, but the core is 5.10 and 5.11, and many of those test balance and footwork rather than strength. Lines begin right off the ground and head toward a big central alcove. A quiet, technical corner that suits intermediate climbers polishing slab skills and stronger ones wanting thin, precise moves. Rock between the lines is patchier than on the quarry's main wall.

ca_trigantor.blurb: Trigantor is a single big boulder in the Rainbow bouldering area beside I-80 near Big Bend, in the Donner and Truckee zone of the Tahoe region. It is split into three tall wedge-shaped blocks with a chimney between them, and the problems are largely cracks and highballs. About seventeen lines cover a very wide range, from beginner V0 and V1 hand cracks through mid-grade problems to a few seriously hard V8 and V9 lines. A short scramble up a trail from the road leads to its base, and the top-out descent is a downclimb along the spine of one wedge. Traffic noise from the interstate carries up to the boulders.

ca_stonehenge_boulders.blurb: Stonehenge Boulders is a small, quiet cluster of high-desert blocks on the east side of Sunset Cliffs near Apple Valley, reached from the Horsemen's Center trailhead along the south edge of the cemetery. Its seventeen problems are mostly low-grade, running from VB through V2, with just a few harder lines up to V5. Many are slabby, around fifteen to twenty feet tall, and reward careful footwork and balance over power. The rock is solid but not polished. Bring several pads for the sloping landings. Late fall through early spring is the comfortable window; summer heat makes it unpleasant. Expect solitude and wide desert views.

ca_sabres_of_paradise.blurb: Sabres of Paradise is a steep, mostly shaded wall of pocketed volcanic boulder problems on the west rim of the Happy Boulders, in the Volcanic Tablelands outside Bishop. A long traverse crosses the face, with a number of up-problems starting from it and from a wedged block in the alcove, plus an easier traverse to the right. Seventeen problems cover a broad spread, from V0 and V1 warm-ups through the mid-grades to several V7 and V8 test pieces and one V9. The west rim tends to feel cooler and less busy than the middle of the canyon. Sits between the Highbrow and Hand to Hand Combat areas.

ca_south_face_left_side.blurb: The left side of Tahquitz Rock's South Face lies just right of the Open Book area at around 7,000 feet above Idyllwild. Reach it by heading right from Lunch Rock and following the trail as it wraps around the cliff. This is mostly traditional climbing on cracks and water-pocketed face, with routes of up to four pitches and a few top-rope options. Grades run from an approachable 5.6 up to a 5.12, with most of the seventeen lines between 5.8 and 5.12 and a good number in the 5.11 range. A solid mix of moderate classics and hard multi-pitch climbs on pale, sun-exposed rock.

ca_sorcerer_the.blurb: The Sorcerer is one of the big spires in the Needles above the Kern River in the southern Sierra, at roughly 7,600 feet. Its steep east face carries many of the area's best multi-pitch trad routes, while the upper west face has a few shorter lines and the glowing Fire Wall below holds hard one-pitch test pieces. Seventeen routes are listed, mostly trad with a couple of sport lines, and the grades start around 5.10 with the bulk at 5.11 and a few 5.12s. Most routes are reached by dropping through the narrow gap between the Sorcerer and the Witch and following a long ramp along the base. Descent usually involves a long rappel.
